questions.question: What is the name of the force with which earth pulls everything towards itself?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gravity.**__

__
 
• **Gravity **is the **force** by which a **planet or other body** draws** objects toward its center**.
 
• The force of **gravity keeps all of the planets in orbit around the sun.**
 
• **Anything that has mass also has gravity.** Objects with **more mass** have **more gravity.** Gravity also gets** weaker with distance**. So, the **closer objects** are to each other, the** stronger their gravitational pull** is.
 
• **Earth's gravity **comes from all its** mass. **
 
• All its** mass** makes a combined** gravitational pull **on all the **mass in an object **in its gravitational area.
 
• This **gravitational pull** causes an **object to come back to earth** if we t**hrow it up in the air.**
 
• We experience **weight **because for the same reason. And if we were on** a planet with less mass than Earth**, we would** weigh less than we do on earth.** That's the reason why our **weight on the moon becomes 1/6th of our weight on earth.**
 
• The **planets revolve around the sun** because of the** gravitational force **between the **sun and the planet.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Thrust:**

 
 
• The force acting **perpendicular to the surface of the object is called thrust.**
 
• When any object is put into the water then the object will replace the water the same as its volume and the cause of which there is a force acting upwards, to balance this weight is called the thrust force.
 
• The effect of thrust is more on the smaller surface area than the thrust acting on a larger surface area. 
 
• **Thrust Force (FT) = Pressure (P) × Area (A)**
 
 
 
• **Resistance:**
 
 
• The resistance of a metal conductor is always directly proportional to its length as the longer the conductor, the more will be its resistance.
 
• **Resistance = Resistivity × Length / Area**

__
 
• 
 **Conductor__**

 __
 
• 
 
**​__**A substance or material that permits the flow of electricity is known as an electrical conductor. When voltage is provided, electrical charge carriers, often electrons or ions, travel effortlessly from atom to atom in a conductor.

 
 
• 
 
Several types of electrical conductors include - Human Body, Copper, Aluminium, Silver, Gold, Graphite, Platinum.

 
 
• 
 
Electric charges can easily pass through an electrical conductor. Conductivity is the ability of conductors to "conduct" electricity. Such materials provide less barrier to the movement of charges. Because electrons can freely flow through conducting materials, charge transfer is simple. Such materials offer less opposition or “resistance” to the flow of charges. Conducting materials allows easy charge transfer because of the free movement of electrons through them.

 
 
 
 
• **__Electrical Conductor Properties__**
 __
 
• 
 
The flow of electrons and ions via a conductor is constant.

 
 
• 
 
Since there is no electric field inside a conductor, electrons can move around freely.

 
 
• 
 
Inside a conductor, the charge density is zero.

 
 
• 
 
Free charges are only present on the conductor's surface.

 
 
• 
 
A conductor's points are all at the same potential.

 
 
• 
 
Many metals are effective electrical conductors. This is the rationale behind the use of metals in electrical appliance parts. Insulators are the plastic casings that shield electrical conductors. We won't experience an electric shock thanks to it.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Non-Metallic Conductor: Graphite
 
• Alloy Conductor: Brass, Bronze, etc.
 
• __**Liquid Conductor**__
 
• Metallic Conductor: Mercury
 
• Non Metallic Conductor: Saline Water, Acid Solution, etc.
 
• Copper Conductor is the most common material used for electrical wiring.
 
• Gold Conductor is used for high-quality surface-to-surface contacts.
 
• Silver is the best conductor on the Conductors list.
 
• Impure Water is listed in the Conductor List but it has less conductivity.

• **Ammeter **is used for measuring **electrical current.**

questions.question: Nuclear fusion reaction is based on which of the following equation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nuclear Fusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d75abffb1d7f21a0cb21fc40907655c03b3b6a401e1a3b03d94c609e009dc398.png] 

 
• Nuclear fusion is the process in which two light nuclei fuse or join together to form a larger nucleus.
 
• During this process, some of the mass of the fusing nuclei is converted to energy which is released. 
 
• Fusion is the process that powers active stars, releasing large quantities of energy.
 
• The origin of the energy released in the fusion of light elements is due to an interplay of two opposing forces: the nuclear force that draws together protons and neutrons and the Coulomb force that causes protons to repel each other. 
 
• The protons are positively charged and repel each other, but they nonetheless stick together, demonstrating the existence of another force referred to as nuclear attraction. This force, called the strong nuclear force, overcomes electric repulsion in a very close range.
 
• The difference in mass is released as energy according to Albert Einstein’s mass-energy equivalence formula

 E =mc2 . 

 
• If the input nuclei are sufficiently massive, the resulting fusion product will be heavier than the sum of the reactants’ original masses, in which case the reaction requires an external source of energy.
 
• The dividing line between “light” and “heavy” is iron-56. Above this atomic mass, energy will generally be released by nuclear fission reactions; below this mass, energy will be released by fusion.

questions.question: Kinetic and potential energies of a body are the components of its ______ energy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Mechanical.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The kinetic and potential energies of a body are the components of its mechanical energy.
 
• Mechanical Energy:
 
 
• The sum of potential energy and kinetic energy is called mechanical energy.
 
• From the above, it is clear that the total mechanical energy is the sum of potential energy and kinetic energy.
 
 

 
• **Potential Energy:**

 
 
• The energy of an object obtained by doing work against conservative forces like spring force and gravitational force is called potential energy.
 
• The potential energy of an object at a height from the ground is given as:
 
 
• **P = mgh**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• The energy obtained by an object by virtue of its motion is called kinetic energy.
 
 
• **KE = (1)/(2) times mv²**
 
 
 
• K is kinetic energy, v is the speed of the object, and m is the mass of the object.

questions.question: Which of the following is a poor conductor of electricity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Distilled water**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Distilled water** is a poor conductor of electricity.
 
• This is because distilled water is free from salts and minerals that can carry electric current.
 
• On the other hand, **tap water, pond water, and hand pump water** contain dissolved salts and minerals, making them better conductors of electricity.
 
• Conductivity in water is primarily due to the presence of ions, which are absent in distilled water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrolytes** in water, such as salts, acids, and bases, dissociate into ions that facilitate the conduction of electricity.
 
• Pure water, such as distilled water, lacks these electrolytes, and thus, has very low conductivity.
 
• In practical applications, water conductivity is often used as an indicator of water purity.
 
• Water with high conductivity is generally considered less pure due to the presence of dissolved substances.

questions.question: What is the unit of measurement for optical power of the lens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diopter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The diopter (D) is the unit of measurement for the optical power of a lens or curved mirror.
 
• It is defined as the reciprocal of the focal length (f) measured in meters (i.e., D = 1/f).
 
• A lens with a focal length of 1 meter has an optical power of 1 diopter.
 
• Lenses with positive diopters are converging lenses, while those with negative diopters are diverging lenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Optical Power:**

 
 
• Optical power, also known as lens power, is the degree to which a lens converges or diverges light.
 
• It is an important concept in optics and is essential in the design of optical systems such as glasses, cameras, and telescopes.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length:**
 
 
• The focal length of a lens is the distance from the lens at which parallel rays of light converge to a single point.
 
• It determines the magnifying power of the lens and is crucial in the formation of clear images.
 
 
 
• **Converging and Diverging Lenses:**
 
 
• Converging lenses (positive diopters) focus light to a point and are used in applications like magnifying glasses and corrective lenses for hyperopia (farsightedness).
 
• Diverging lenses (negative diopters) spread light outwards and are used in devices like peepholes and corrective lenses for myopia (nearsightedness).

__
 
• **Sunlight consists of seven colours**__.
 
• The **sunlight **splits into seven colours namely violet, indigo, blue, green, orange, and red.
 __
 
• We usually call it** VIBGYOR**.
 
• When we mix all these colours we just get one light which is the **WHITE light**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sunlight is a portion of the electromagnetic radiation given off by the Sun, in particular infrared, visible, and ultraviolet light.
 
• On Earth, sunlight is scattered and filtered through Earth's atmosphere and is obvious as daylight when the Sun is above the horizon.
 
• When direct solar radiation is not blocked by clouds, it is experienced as sunshine, a combination of bright light and radiant heat.
 
• When blocked by clouds or reflected off other objects, sunlight is diffused.
 
• Sources estimate a global average of between** 164 watts to 340 watts per square meter over a 24-hour day**; this figure is estimated by NASA to be about a quarter of Earth's average total solar irradiance.

questions.question: Which of the following groups is a good conductor of heat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Steel, copper and aluminium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Conductor**: 

 
 
• A **substance **or **material **that **permits the flow of electricity **is known as an **electrical conductor**.
 
• When voltage **is provided**, **electrical charge carriers**, often electrons or ions, travel **effortlessly from atom to atom in a conductor**.
 
• **Materials made **of **metal **are common **electrical conductors**.
 
• On the **surface of conductors**, there is **an electric charge**.
 
• There are **four different kinds of conductors**: **semiconductors, resistors, excellent conductors, and non-conductors**.
 
• Some **examples of conductors**: **Silver, Gold, Copper, Aluminum, Mercury, Steel, Iron, and Seawater**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Semiconductor**:

 
 
• An **item made of silicon **that conducts electricity more **than an insulator **like **glass **but less **than a pure conductor **like **copper or aluminium is known as a semiconductor**.
 
• A **semiconductor **material has an **electrical conductivity **value falling **between that of a conductor and an insulator**.
 
• Its **resistivity falls **as **its temperature rises**; metals **behave in the opposite way**.
 
• Some **examples of semiconductors **are **silicon, germanium, gallium arsenide etc**.
 
 
 
• **Insulator**:
 
 
• **Any material **that **keeps energy **such as electricity, heat, or cold from easily transferring through is an insulator.
 
• A **substance that prevents the free flow of electrical current **is known as an **electrical insulator**.
 
• The **electrons in the insulator's atoms **are securely **bonded and immobile**.
 
• **Wood, plastic, rubber, and glass are good insulators**.

questions.question: If 7 N force is applied on a brick and it moves through 5 m, then what will be the work done?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**35 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Work is calculated using the formula: **Work = Force × Displacement × cos(θ)**, where θ is the angle between the force and displacement.
 
• Here, the force applied is **7 N**, and the displacement is **5 m**.
 
• If the force and displacement are in the same direction, cos(θ) = cos(0°) = 1.
 
• Thus, Work = 7 × 5 × 1 = **35 J**.
 
• The unit of work in the SI system is the **joule (J)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work:**

 
 
• Work is done when a force is applied to an object, and the object moves in the direction of the force.
 
• It is a scalar quantity, meaning it has magnitude but no direction.
 
• The formula for work (W) is **W = F × d × cos(θ)**, where:
 
 
• F = Force applied (N)
 
• d = Displacement (m)
 
• θ = Angle between the force and displacement
 
 
 
 
 
• **Joule:**
 
 
• The joule (J) is the SI unit of work and energy.
 
• **1 joule is equivalent to 1 newton-meter (N·m)**.
 
• It represents the work done when a force of 1 newton displaces an object by 1 meter in the direction of the force.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Work:**
 
 
• The magnitude of the force applied.
 
• The displacement caused by the force.
 
• The angle between the force and the displacement.
 
 
 
• **Work in Different Systems:**
 
 
• In the CGS system, the unit of work is the erg.
 
• **1 erg = 10⁻⁷ joules.**

questions.question: Which law is also known as the law of inertia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The law that is also known as the law of inertia is Newton's First Law of Motion.**
 
• It states that an object at rest tends to **stay at rest, and an object in motion tends to stay in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an external force.**
 
• This fundamental law of **physics was formulated by Sir Isaac Newton** and is one of the three laws that form the basis of classical mechanics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion, also known as the law of acceleration, describes the relationship between the force acting on an object, the mass of the object, and the resulting acceleration.**

 
 
• It is one of the fundamental principles of classical mechanics formulated by Sir Isaac Newton.
 
 
 
• **Archimedes' principle states that when an object is placed in a fluid (like water), it experiences an upward force called buoyant force.**
 
 
• This force is equal to the weight of the fluid that the object displaces (pushes aside).
 
• 
 
**Example - **when you put something in water, it feels a push from the water that tries to lift it up. The more water the object pushes away, the stronger the push (buoyant force) it feels. If the object is lighter than the water it displaces, it will float because the buoyant force is greater than the weight of the object. If the object is heavier, it will sink because the weight is greater than the buoyant force.

 
 
 
 
• **Kepler's laws are a set of three fundamental principles that describe the motion of planets and other celestial objects around the Sun. **Here's a simplified explanation of each law:
 
 
• **Law of Orbits:** Each planet in our solar system moves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit, with the Sun at one of the two foci of the ellipse. In simpler terms, the path of a planet is not a perfect circle but more like a stretched-out circle with the Sun slightly off-center.
 
• **Law of Areas: **An imaginary line connecting a planet to the Sun sweeps out equal areas in equal time intervals. In other words, as a planet moves in its elliptical orbit, it covers an equal area in space over equal periods of time. This means that a planet moves faster when it is closer to the Sun and slower when it is farther away.
 
• **Law of Periods: **The square of the time period of a planet's orbit is proportional to the cube of its average distance from the Sun. In simpler terms, the time it takes for a planet to complete one orbit around the Sun (its period) is related to its average distance from the Sun. The farther a planet is from the Sun, the longer its orbital period.

questions.question: What is the frequency (f) of a wave with a period of 0.04 seconds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The frequency (f) of a wave is the reciprocal of its period (T).
 
• The formula to calculate frequency is f = 1/T.
 
• Given the period T = 0.04 seconds, applying the formula gives f = 1/0.04.
 
• Therefore, the frequency of the wave is f = 25 Hz.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frequency (f)**:

 
 
• Frequency is the number of complete wave cycles that pass a point per unit of time, typically measured in Hertz (Hz).
 
• 1 Hz is equal to one cycle per second.
 
 
 
• **Period (T)**:
 
 
• The period is the time taken for one complete cycle of the wave to pass a given point.
 
• It is usually measured in seconds (s).
 
 
 
• **Relationship between Period and Frequency**:
 
 
• The period is the inverse of the frequency: T = 1/f.
 
• Similarly, frequency is the inverse of the period: f = 1/T.
 
 
 
• **Wave Cycles**:
 
 
• A wave cycle consists of one complete wave oscillation, typically measured from crest to crest or trough to trough.

• **Rolling friction** is defined as the force which resists the motion of a ball or wheel and is the weakest type of friction.
 
• **Fluid friction** is defined as the friction that exists between the layers of the fluid when they are moving relative to each other.

The correct answer is __**Force**__.

__
 
• **Force is the external agency applied on a body to change its state of rest or uniform motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's first law of motion:**

 
 
• Newton's first law states that if a body is at rest or moving at a constant speed in a straight line, it will remain at rest or keep moving in a straight line at constant speed unless it is acted upon by a force.
 
 
• This postulate is known as the law of inertia.
 
 
 
• The law of inertia was first formulated by Galileo Galilei for horizontal motion on Earth and was later generalized by René Descartes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In thermodynamics, **heat** is energy in transfer to or from a thermodynamic system, by mechanisms other than thermodynamic work or transfer of matter.

questions.question: What is the value of g? (g stands for acceleration due to gravitational force of the earth)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9.8 m/s**__**²**.

__
 
• **Acceleration due to gravity** is the acceleration gained by an object due to gravitational force. Its SI unit is **m/s²**.

 
 
• It has both **magnitude and direction, hence, it’s a vector quantity**.
 
• Acceleration due to gravity is **represented by g**.
 
• The standard value of g on the surface of the earth at sea level is **9.8 m/s²**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravity is the force** with which the earth attracts a body towards its centre.

 
 
• The gravity of Earth, which is denoted by g, refers to the acceleration that the Earth imparts to objects on or near its surface.
 
• In SI units this acceleration is measured in meters per second squared (in symbols, m/s²) or equivalently in newtons per kilogram (N/kg).
 
• It has an approximate value of 9.81 m/s², which means that ignoring the effects of air resistance, the speed of an object falling freely near the Earth's surface will increase by about 9.81 meters (32.2 ft) per second every second.
 
• This quantity is sometimes referred to informally as little g (in contrast, the gravitational constant G is referred to as big G).
 
• There is a direct relationship between
 
 
• **gravitational acceleration and the downwards force (weight) experienced by objects on Earth, **given by the equation **F = ma (force = mass × acceleration)**.
 
 
 
• However, other factors such as the rotation of the Earth also contribute to the net acceleration.
 
• The precise strength of Earth's gravity varies depending on location.
 
• The nominal "average" value at the Earth's surface, known as standard gravity is, by definition, 9.80665 m/s² (about 32.1740 ft/s²).

questions.question: In a resistor, what happens to the current when the resistance is doubled?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The current gets halved.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The obstruction to current flow is electrical resistance**.
 
• This implies that when r**esistance is lower, current will be higher**.
 
• **Ohm's Law** states that the **current (I) flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference (V)** across it.
 
• ** V = I R**, where **R **is the conductor's** resistance**
 
• It can also be written as ,
 
• ** I = V/R,**
 
• This means that if **resistance doubles, current will decrease by half because current and resistance have an inverse relationship**.
 
• SI unit of resistance is **Ohm (****Ω)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistor**

 
 
• A **resistor is a passive electrical component having two terminals that control or limits the passage of electric current in electrical circuits**.
 
• Resistors come in a **variety of sizes and forms**.
 
• There are two popular types: **through-hole and surface mount**.
 
• A resistor might be **static, conventional, unique, or part of a set of variable resistors**.
 
 
 
• **Application of Resistor**
 
 
• When a**ccurate measurement, high sensitivity, and balanced current regulation are needed**, wire wound resistors are used in applications like shunt with ampere metres.
 
• **Flame detectors, burglar alarms, photographic equipment**, etc. all use photoresistors.
 
• **Temperature and voltmeter control** is accomplished by resistors.
 
• **Amplifiers, telephony, oscillators, and digital multimeters** all use resistors.
 
• Additionally, they are utilised in** transmitters, demodulators, and modulators**.
